questions.q: Why did Passepartout come running back from the clergyman's house?
choices: The clergyman had refused to marry them
He found out that the day was really Saturday
He had lost his hat and money in the crowded street
He saw Fix waiting outside the Reform Club

questions.q: What did Fogg promise the cabman to hurry him to the club?
choices: A hundred pounds
Twenty shillings
A new carriage
Five hundred pounds
questions.evidence: promised a hundred pounds to the cabman

questions.q: Why had Fogg gained a whole day without knowing it?
choices: His watch had been set wrong in Hong Kong
He had travelled always eastward, toward the sun
He had slept through a day on the Henrietta
The Liverpool clocks were set a day behind
questions.evidence: because he had travelled constantly eastward

questions.q: What did Fogg do with the thousand pounds left after his expenses?
choices: He gave it all to Aouda as a wedding gift
He split it between Passepartout and Fix
He paid it back to the Bank of England at once
He kept it to start a new wager at the club
questions.evidence: He divided the one thousand pounds that remained between Passepartout and the unfortunate Fix

questions.q: Why did Fogg take the cost of the gas out of Passepartout's share?
choices: He was angry about the lost day
For the sake of regularity
He needed the money to pay the cabman
Passepartout asked him to do it

questions.q: Fogg was "as tranquil and phlegmatic as ever." What does phlegmatic mean here?
choices: Excited and loud
Calm and unemotional
Sick and feverish
Proud and boastful
questions.evidence: as tranquil and phlegmatic as ever

questions.q: Why did Fogg tell Aouda that his fortune belonged to her?
choices: The law said a husband's money went to his wife
Her idea of marriage led to finding his mistake in time
She had paid for the special train to London out of her own purse
He no longer wanted to be rich after such a long journey
questions.evidence: If you had not suggested our marriage, my servant would not have gone to the Reverend Samuel Wilson's

questions.q: According to the last lines, what did Fogg truly gain from his journey?
choices: A fine new house and great fame in London
A wife who made him the happiest of men
A new respect for the Reform Club rules
Many friends in every country he visited
questions.evidence: made him the happiest of men
